title: Tuba versus sousaphone and his chops

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Well, did they play -- what's the difference between a tuba and a sousaphone? Is there any?
There's no difference, both of them are tubas. I look at the sousaphone like the baby grand of the tubas.
You'd get a better tone out of it?

How do you get your chops together on tuba? You said you hadn't played for about 30 years, and your chops hadn't gone away. But it seems like such a difficult instrument to play, filling all that with -- all that tubing with wind.

Yes. Oh, I don't know, I just had -- might as well say I just had strong chops. Many a time I was in that military band I was in, that 1924 band, a lot of times we'd go on marching jobs, and I'd be the only tuba in the band.
That takes a lot of stamina, and stuff like that.
Yeah, I know. It just came natural to me. I didn't have a bit of problem, just blew.
